about: A recording's name, made safe for the filesystem it will be written to.
notes: Windows rules, because they are the strictest of the platforms LiberCast ships for and a name that satisfies them satisfies the others.
Path separators become spaces rather than being deleted, so `Film 1/2` does not become `Film 12`.
Cut to 120 bytes, not 120 characters: filesystem limits are in bytes, and a cut by character count can land halfway through a multi-byte one.

cases.name: path separators become spaces
cases.why: Deleting them would turn `Film 1/2` into `Film 12`, which is a different title rather than a safe one.

cases.name: trailing dots and spaces are dropped
cases.why: Windows strips them on create and then cannot find the file it just wrote.

cases.name: a reserved device name is given a suffix
cases.why: `CON` is not a filename on Windows, it is the console.

cases.name: reserved names are matched whatever the case
a name merely containing a reserved word is fine
a name that sanitises to nothing gets one
cases.why: An empty filename is not a filename, and failing the recording at this point would lose it.

cases.name: an empty name gets one too
accented characters are kept
cases.why: They are legal and they are the name. Stripping them would mangle most of the Turkish and German catalogue.
